finding.claim: A binary DER public key passed as a Buffer is accepted as an HMAC secret when `algorithms` is omitted or includes HS*, enabling HS256 forgery with the public key. Precondition: operator passes a DER public key as a Buffer and does not pin `algorithms` to asymmetric algorithms. Severity: medium.
finding.source: Attacker holds the public key bytes (public by design) and crafts a token with alg HS256 signed with those bytes.
finding.sink: verifySignature HS branch (src/crypto.js:396-399) using the DER bytes as an HMAC key.

trace.note: detectPublicKeyAlgorithms(key, allowedAlgorithms) called with the Buffer; key checks at 512-544 pass for a non-empty Buffer.
HS-only shortcut skipped because allowedAlgorithms is empty.
Buffer decoded as UTF-8, turning DER into replacement characters.
locatePem finds no '-----BEGIN' header, so isRawSecret=true.
assertNotAsymmetricJwkJson only checks JSON/JWK, so DER passes.
Returns hsAlgorithms.
allowedAlgorithms becomes HS256/384/512.
prepareKeyOrSecret makes a secret KeyObject from the raw DER Buffer (src/verifier.js:41).
HMAC over token input with the DER bytes, compared via timingSafeEqual (398).

finding.guards_checked: none-only gating (verifier.js:513-527) n/a; empty-key check (verifier.js:533-544) passes; asymmetric JWK refusal (crypto.js:143-147) only covers JSON/JWK; PEM locator (crypto.js:130-138) finds no header; algorithm allowlist (verifier.js:170) is derived from the key so HS is allowed. Not affected when algorithms is pinned to RS*/PS*/ES*/EdDSA: checkAreCompatibleAlgorithms (verifier.js:551, crypto.js:20-32) throws invalidKey.

finding.claim: The base64url check does not enforce canonical encoding of the signature segment's trailing bits, so one signature maps to several token strings. This contradicts the invariant stated at src/verifier.js:174-176. Exploitable only if the application keys replay protection, one-time use, or a denylist on the raw token string rather than jti. Severity: low-medium.
finding.source: Attacker alters the unused trailing bits of the last character of the signature segment of a valid token.
finding.sink: Acceptance of a non-canonical token string through verifySignature (src/crypto.js:394, 398), which returns the payload.

trace.note: signatureSegment is the text after the last '.'.
BASE64URL_RE = /^[A-Za-z0-9_-]*$/ checks only the alphabet.
Signature segment passes the alphabet check unchanged.
Signature passed through unchanged.
verifySignature runs because signature is non-empty.
Buffer.from(signature,'base64') discards trailing bits, so decoded bytes are unchanged.
timingSafeEqual passes; payload returned at verifier.js:432/477.

finding.guards_checked: Alphabet check (decoder.js:41); HMAC/signature comparison on decoded bytes (crypto.js:398); header and payload are covered by the signature over the exact string (verifier.js:403), so only the signature segment is malleable; verifier cache keyed by hash of full token (utils.js:45-59), so the cache is not the issue. Variants: 4 for HS256 (43-char signature, 2 unused bits), 16 for RS256/ES256 (4 unused bits).

finding.claim: The asymmetric-JWK refusal checks only the first character of the trimmed key. A leading character that String.trim() does not remove (e.g. U+200B or NUL) lets a serialized public JWK fall through to HMAC. Same class as GHSA-g3jj-5cmm-3hxx; the PEM path was hardened against this (crypto.js:33-39) but the JWK path was not. Precondition: algorithms omitted or includes HS*, and the attacker knows the exact key bytes including the prefix. Severity: low; not reproduced at runtime.
finding.source: Operator passes a serialized public JWK/JWKS string that begins with such a character.
finding.sink: HMAC key built from the raw JWK string (crypto.js:227 / verifier.js:556).

trace.note: trimmedKey = key.trim(), which keeps U+200B and NUL.
isRawSecret=true, so assertNotAsymmetricJwkJson(trimmedKey) runs.
firstChar is not '{' or '[', so returns false without parsing.
Treated as hsAlgorithms.

finding.guards_checked: PEM locator tolerates leading junk (crypto.js:40, 130-138), but applies to PEM only; JSON/JWK parse on '{' or '[' (crypto.js:109-121) is bypassed by the prefix; algorithm pinning as in F1.

finding.claim: With the cache enabled, a Buffer token passes the type check but throws a TypeError in the cache key builder, so verify() throws a non-TokenError instead of a classified rejection. Fail-closed, so no auth bypass; impact is a non-TokenError (possible 500 or misclassification) for apps that branch on err.code. Severity: low.
finding.source: Caller passes a Buffer token (accepted at verifier.js:361 and decoder.js:14-15).
finding.sink: hashToken calls token.split() on a Buffer (src/utils.js:46).

trace.note: Buffer accepted by the type guard.
cacheKeyBuilder(token) is called before decode.
token.split('.', 1) throws TypeError: split is not a function.
No try/catch, so the TypeError escapes verify() in both sync and async modes.

finding.guards_checked: Type guard (verifier.js:361) accepts Buffer; decoder Buffer handling (decoder.js:14-15) works but runs only after the cache lookup; cache is disabled by default (verifier.js:612-614, createCache returns null).
